text:
andrew: Quick sync — pulled together the pelican9b quant runs. key slices: multi-turn summarization (news->Q/A), code completion, and casual chat. results look... promising but noisy on priming sensitivity.

sara: nice. can you drop the perf/cost numbers?

andrew: sure. TL;DR: int8 reduces latency ~18% vs fp16, int4 reduces cost ~36% vs int8 but some acc drift on long multi-turn. raw numbers from our microbench:
```
fp16: p95=220ms, tokens/sec=90, cost/unit=$0.012
int8: p95=180ms, tokens/sec=105, cost/unit=$0.0095
int4: p95=170ms, tokens/sec=110, cost/unit=$0.0061
```
note: costs are normalized per-token using our current GPU price sheet.

kai: what about quality? any regression metrics for the summarization slice?

andrew: yes. paired BLEU/ROUGE aren't great for multi-turn, so we used a targeted hallucination check + user-intent pass rate. summary:
- fp16: hallucination rate 3.2%, intent-pass 93.5%
- int8: hallucination 3.6%, intent-pass 92.8%
- int4: hallucination 6.9% (up), intent-pass 88.1% (down)

mira: hmm int4 looks risky for that slice. where is the signal coming from? priming tokens?

andrew: exactly. the degradation correlates with long instruction prefixes (>120 tokens) and reused KV cache patterns across turns. int4's quant noise amplifies prefix drift.

olivia: do we have a per-slice unit-econ estimate if we route 70% traffic to int4 and 30% to int8 as a hybrid?

andrew: quick calc: assume baseline traffic = 1M tokens/day. using cost/unit above:
- hybrid (70% int4, 30% int8): 0.7*0.0061 + 0.3*0.0095 = $0.00728/token avg -> $7,280/day
- all-int8: 1.0*0.0095 = $9,500/day
- all-fp16: $12,000/day
So hybrid saves ~23% vs all-int8 and ~39% vs fp16.

sara: but quality hit matters. if 70% int4 causes user-visible regressions on multi-turn, product will push back. Any middle-ground?

kai: what about dynamic per-request routing by priming length / user intent? short prompts -> int4, long multi-turn -> int8. cheap rule engine.

andrew: did a quick classifier threshold on prefix length + avg token reuse; routing accuracy ~92% (on our validation slices). That would route ~60% of traffic to int4 while keeping most risky sessions on int8.

mira: that sounds safer. do we have rollout plan & canary?

andrew: proposed rollout:
1) Canary 5% traffic to hybrid routing (rules only) for 48h, monitor intent-pass and NPS proxy (satisfaction proxies we capture).
2) If no regression >1.5% absolute on intent-pass, move to 25% for 72h.
3) Full hybrid at 60% after 1 week of clean metrics.

olivia: ops ask: on Dedicated we can pin some sessions to int4 nodes. any infra blockers?

ops-bot: note: current autoscaler config needs a new "quant-variant" label to place int4 workloads on Q4 queues. file a PR to eng-infra for helm chart change.

kai: for product/GTN guidance: recommend offering "economy" tier that uses hybrid routing with warning about long sessions and an "SLA" tier pinned to int8/fp16. that gives GTN clear choices.

sara: agree. also prepare a short scorecard for GTN: include p95 latency, cost per 1M tokens, intent-pass delta vs fp16, and example failure cases (long priming/regression examples).

andrew: I'll assemble the scorecard and a small snippet of failing transcripts (anonymized) + the routing rule config. aiming to hand off by EOD tomorrow.

mira: quick ask — can we run a targeted human eval on 200 multi-turn threads (mix of short/long) for int4 vs int8? automated metrics may miss subtle fluency drops.

andrew: yes scheduled. will queue a human-eval batch for tomorrow morning; should finish in 24h.

olivia: thanks team. seems like a conservative hybrid route + routing-by-prefix is the recommended path. GTN: expect a short one-pager + scorecard tomorrow.

andrew: ping @sara @kai when scorecard ready for review :thumbsup:

ops-bot: deploy note: canary flag created: feature/pelican9b-hybrid-route.helm -> pending eng-infra PR for quant-variant label.
